verdict: Fail: substantial revision required. The taxonomy closely fits most discovery tasks, but it omits in-distribution code synthesis, undercovers two guideposts, duplicates a version-control capability, contains several non-transferable catch-alls, and has invalid prerequisite edges.
blocking_findings: Coverage: all six C01 HumanEvalPlus/MBPPPlus probes (eval-01 through eval-06) require standalone function synthesis, yet c01 explicitly excludes algorithm exercises detached from a software system and no leaf covers them. This also undercuts guidepost C01.1, Code synthesis from spec. These probes are held-out coverage evidence, not generation evidence, but the contradiction is direct.

Coverage: guidepost C01.6, Build packaging & dependency management, is reduced to optional-import availability in c01.5.1. There is no leaf for build configuration, package construction, dependency constraints or resolution, lockfile maintenance, or release artifacts. Similarly, C01.7, Version control operations, is reduced to application-controlled staging in c01.5.2 while branching, merging, rebasing, conflict resolution, and history manipulation are explicitly excluded or absent.

Boundary: c01.2.3.2 and c01.5.2 claim essentially the same capability. Both trace an automatic-staging setting, separate generation from staging, test enabled and disabled modes, and use c01-d15 as their representative case. There is no decisive operation that assigns the DVC task to one rather than the other; these sections should be merged or given genuinely distinct outcomes.

Coverage/boundary: c01-d09 is restoration of an existing public API contract, but c01.3 excludes repairs that restore existing contracts. Its apparent destination, c01.3.1.1, rewrites the task as adding a new option. The corrective-maintenance leaves do not cover public-signature or output-format regressions, so the discovery task has no valid primary leaf.

Generation: the c01 representative probe is an omnibus rather than a coherent task. It conjoins diagnosis of a configuration defect, a schema-backed asynchronous feature, caller refactoring, optional-dependency work, version-control integration, and two levels of testing. These operations need not arise from one change and cannot isolate the claimed root capability. The c01.2.3 representative similarly forces lifecycle-event restoration and repository staging into one pipeline despite those being independent discovery capabilities.
mutual_confidence_findings: c01.2.1.1 fails mutual confidence. Counterexample pair: c01-d02 requires deriving half-open interval overlap semantics; c01-d03 requires understanding Python compile modes and namespace evaluation. Mastery of the interval repair would not predict the compile/eval repair after changing surface form or library.

c01.3.1.1 fails mutual confidence. Counterexample pair: c01-d09 restores a Python formatting parameter and applies string or callable prefixes per line; c01-d14 extends a Rust procedural macro, resolves optionality precedence, and changes generated TypeScript. The compiler-macro and code-generation knowledge is central, not a removable tool detail.

c01.2.3 is too broad. Counterexample pair: c01-d06 reconnects a crawler lifecycle logging hook with ordering and multiplicity constraints; c01-d15 traces configuration into Git-index staging behavior. Mastery of event emission does not predict correct index-state preservation.

c01.3 is a broad catch-all. Counterexample pair: c01-d05 designs and normalizes grouped dataframe aggregation specifications; c01-d01 implements asynchronous lease acquisition, renewal, cancellation, and leadership callbacks. Their central operations and prerequisite knowledge do not transfer.

c01.5 fails mutual confidence. Counterexample pair: c01-d04 separates annotation-time imports from optional-runtime availability; c01-d15 preserves Git index state under an autostaging configuration. Combining them in a hypothetical plugin task does not create transfer between dependency loading and version-control semantics.
continuity_findings: Edge c01.1.1 -> c01.1.2.1 is unnecessary. The dependent representative task is a parameterized range-relation suite whose contract is already supplied; it does not require the full prerequisite outcome of tracing entry points, dispatch, state, and side effects.

Edge c01.1 -> c01.3.3 has too large an entry delta. Adapting a blocking lock acquisition into a cancellable asynchronous method introduces nonblocking adaptation, event-loop execution, cancellation behavior, concurrency races, and lock-result preservation, none of which is modeled by repository investigation and behavioral evidence.

Edge c01.3.1.1 -> c01.3.1.2 is not necessary and does not yield a minimal delta. A bounded formatting or declarative-attribute extension does not supply grouped-aggregation semantics, selector normalization, output naming, or result-shape rules required by the dependent entry task.

Edge c01.3.1.1 -> c01.3.4 is unnecessary. Creating two modules with a one-way import and tested wrapper does not require mastery of parameter or attribute parsing, precedence, and per-item output propagation.

Edge c01.4.1 -> c01.4.2 is unnecessary for the stated entry task. Renaming one parameter and updating callers and tests does not require the full structure-preserving-refactoring outcome of module extraction, duplication removal, export maintenance, and dependency-direction control.
All 46 prerequisite edges were checked; the remaining 41 have a plausible necessity relationship and an entry task with a reasonably bounded delta.
other_findings: Evidence gap: the supplied discovery and evaluation annotations contain semantic keys but no task-to-section mappings, retrieval scores, or neighbor stability. Mapping quality therefore cannot be evaluated independently.

Discovery evidence is strong for repair subtypes and the sampled feature tasks, but there is no direct discovery example for c01.4 refactoring or interface migration, general build/dependency management, or general version-control operations. Those sections rely on guideposts or curriculum invention rather than discovery support.

Evaluation evidence is narrow: the seven manifest entries listing C01 comprise six standalone function-synthesis probes and one instruction-scheduling multiple-choice probe. They provide no held-out evidence for testing, refactoring, packaging, dependency management, or version-control behavior. Eval-08 also appears closer to computer architecture than repository software engineering, so its C01 applicability is a routing-evidence concern rather than a reason to invent a curriculum leaf.
AAII 4.3 was correctly treated as metadata-only and supplied no generation or coverage evidence.

Structurally, all 30 sections contain exactly one entry and one representative instruction. The internal representatives for c01.1, c01.1.2, c01.2, c01.2.1, c01.2.2, c01.3, c01.3.1, c01.4, and c01.5 can be instantiated as cross-child scenarios; c01 and c01.2.3 have the synthesis failures identified above.
Fifteen of the sixteen discovery tasks have a plausible primary leaf. The exception is c01-d09; c01-d15 instead has two indistinguishable homes.
rubric_changes: Require a cross-subject evidence ledger that assigns every guidepost, discovery task, and permitted evaluation probe one primary section or an explicit exclusion rationale. This would expose silent omissions and duplicate homes without turning held-out probes into generation evidence.

Require a prerequisite-edge audit table recording necessity, which parts of the prerequisite outcome the dependent representative uses, and the single delta introduced by the entry task. This makes the existing progression rule reproducible across subjects.

Clarify mutual confidence for internal nodes: evaluate transfer among tasks assigned directly to the node, while separately requiring its representative probe to instantiate one coherent scenario spanning all children. Explicitly reject representatives formed by merely concatenating unrelated child clauses.
